title: 1. Kinds of stage, and three tiers of change

sections.name: kinds
sections.label: Eight kinds of stage
sections.content:
Expressible today: extract (write records of one type from a source); update (fill fields on records an earlier stage made, though only implied by position); target (fill fields of the one record the run is building: the original design); synthesise (write records that group or judge earlier ones, with the links arriving from them).

Not expressible: for-each (repeat a stage or a sub-protocol per item); compute (derive values with no judgement: counts, rank, render); gate (a person accepts, rejects or promotes); live (a source that is still arriving).

sections.name: tier1
sections.label: Tier 1: fits the spec as it stands
sections.content: Additive optional properties and fixes: a stage's mode; the relations a stage writes; which end RelationSpec.required binds, and a label; what a stage reads; more than one output type and a named uncertainty type; an anchor on SourceReference or the fragment-identifier convention already in use; an explicit Blueprint reference on a Protocol; a meta carrier on definitions; and the filed bugs (srs#1053, srs#1054, srs-rust#1711 to #1714).

sections.name: tier2
sections.label: Tier 2: needs design, inside the Protocol extension
sections.content: A specified ProtocolRun that travels and records what each stage produced; a small vocabulary of checkable completion; records under construction (a required field written by a later stage); gate stages; compute stages; composition (extends, and a sub-run per item); scope (persistent types and standing records outside the document's container).

sections.name: tier3
sections.label: Tier 3: deeper, and wider than the Protocol
sections.content: Context assembly at scale; what a tension or contradiction between records means and who rules on it; provenance across repositories; live protocols and the attention cursor; people as records; what re-running a stage does; withholding as an export.
